reviews.text: The actors, young or old, transform themselves fully to make what some may regard as their “unexamined lives” worth living, worth recounting, and for observers, worth admiring for their internal fortitude, honesty, and resulting sagacity.
reviews.author: Toba Singer

reviews.text: Hirokazu Kore-eda is one of my favorite directors working today and he did not disappoint with Shoplifters.
reviews.author: JD Duran

reviews.text: You feel like you’re watching the lives of real people as the story grows and sprouts. It makes the smaller moments of bonding, such as a trip to the beach, all the more charming. Yet it also makes the eventual truths all the more shocking.
reviews.author: Calum Cooper

reviews.text: The best movies teach you something you may not have already considered, and Shoplifters might do just that for many people, especially families.
reviews.author: Brendan Cassidy

reviews.text: Kore-eda favors the intimate and subtle over big drama, and this film is filled with both touching and heartbreaking moments of affection and disappointment.
reviews.author: Sean Axmaker

reviews.text: Shoplifters is a tender film about a family comprised of thieves, murderers, kidnappers, scammers, and liars.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: Episode 23: Vox Lux / The Guilty / Shoplifters / The Mule / Rififi
reviews.author: Taylor Baker

reviews.text: Director/writer Hirokazu Kore-eda handles the film with a pragmatic yet empathetic eye and as a result, crafts together one of the year's best movies that clutches the heartstrings by the time the credits roll.
reviews.author: Matthew St. Clair

reviews.text: For the underprivileged, the concept of family can be as extended as necessity mandates [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Gisela Savdie

reviews.text: Shoplifters tells a story about love, family, crime, and truth. It's life itself without the morality cloak. One of the best movies of 2018. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Victor Pineyro

reviews.text: Shoplifters shows us that family is simply a concept, a social construct that has little to do with genetics and instead springs from love and sacrifice.
reviews.author: Scott Phillips

reviews.text: Kore-eda offers an intimate view of a poverty-stricken Japanese family from ground level, where the ground is continually cut from underneath their feet.
reviews.author: Prahlad Srihari

reviews.text: This is a harrowing, elegant, and graceful piece of art that is easily one of the best offerings of the year.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: The film supposes another master work in the filmography of the Japanese director, full of periodic emotions and dramatic moments of great intensity of which I leave moved to the guts when I witness a family. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: [SHOPLIFTERS] is top-notch Kore-eda with a Farhadi-esque moral dilemma and fantastic, nuanced filmmaking that never spoon-feeds the audience and presents its story in graceful, absorbing ways.
reviews.author: Mina Takla

reviews.text: While this has the potential of becoming a bleak melodrama, Kore-eda ensures the story retains a sense of poignancy and emotionality.
reviews.author: Katie Smith-Wong

reviews.text: With Shoplifters, Koreeda embarks on an ambitious philosophical journey to explore the fundamentals of family. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Hugo Hernández Valdivia

reviews.text: "Shoplifters" is a genuine Koreeda film, a masterful family drama, and of his best latest works, which definitely says something considering the quality of all of his films.
reviews.author: Panos Kotzathanasis

reviews.text: It's accessible, fluently told and packs an unexpected punch.
reviews.author: Zhuo-Ning Su

reviews.text: Filled with a compassionate, profound and intelligent narrative that never leaves you for a second, Shoplifters is the best film of the year and a perfect swan song to Kirin Kiki who literally gets buried in a Kore-eda household.
reviews.author: Shikhar Verma

reviews.text: A film that just grows and grows and grows. It seems very quiet, but you are absolutely hooked.
reviews.author: Amy Nicholson

reviews.text: Despite the hiding, the brokenness, and the stealing, this family in Shoplifters is a small snapshot of joy, and one that shines a sorely needed light.
reviews.author: Debbie Holloway

reviews.text: This film is perhaps the most unusual heartwarming movie we've seen and it's magical in its own way.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: Kore-eda is less interested in judging this family for their thievery ... than he is in examining their humanity and empathizing with their working-class plight.
reviews.author: Brett McCracken

reviews.text: It's funny and emotional, uplifting and heartbreaking, it's one of the best movies of the year.
reviews.author: Karl Delossantos

reviews.text: There's a musicality to absolutely everything in the film, from petty thieving at corner stores to conversations around a crowded dinner table.
reviews.author: Siddhant Adlakha

reviews.text: [Shoplifters] is a film edged by despair, and yet is life-affirming. Families may disintegrate, but love keeps us ticking over.
reviews.author: Shubhra Gupta

reviews.text: Through a tale about an impoverished family that steals to get by, director Kore-eda questions the very notion of parenthood.
reviews.author: Rashid Irani

reviews.text: Hirokazu Kore-eda's Shoplifters is a layered, textured film and a definite must watch. Make time for it.
reviews.author: Sreeparna Sengupta

reviews.text: It's astonishing the clarity and patience in which Hirokazu Koreeda unveils the truth. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fausto Ponce

reviews.text: Kore-eda explores these questions with a slow, deliberate and damned near-perfect film.
reviews.author: John Bleasdale

reviews.text: Like Hirokazu's best work, it is quiet, hushed, and often unassuming, but lands with power of an earthquake.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: Noone else shooting movies on this planet is so consistently wringing real, genuine and unfakeable emotion out of his scripts and performances as [director Hirokazu] Kore-eda is here.
reviews.author: Graeme Tuckett

reviews.text: Some beautiful moments of joy. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alonso Díaz de la Vega

reviews.text: In Shoplifters, Hirokazu Kore-eda produces an emotional film that transports the audience into the confines of a claustrophobic, cluttered atmosphere; brimming with warmth as he introduces a family of loveable criminals
reviews.author: Sara Clements

reviews.text: These motley individuals have bruised souls. And the pain runs deep. As the film progresses, writer/director Hirokazu Kore-eda parcels out clue after clue.
reviews.author: Stephen Garrett

reviews.text: Kore-eda has long displayed a gift for finding the humanity in his characters.
reviews.author: Phil Guie

reviews.text: Shoplifters shines attention on two phenomena eroding Japan's social foundation: underemployment and gentrification. Most people have jobs, but they're menial and low-paying.
reviews.author: Jorge Ignacio Castillo

reviews.text: A work of deep humanity. You walk away breathless.
reviews.author: Philip Huang

reviews.text: A masterly piece from an auteur who is clearly in a state of grace. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Caviaro

reviews.text: This near masterpiece made me think for long periods of time, meaning that its message and purpose were conveyed with a glorious sense of accomplishment.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: Lily Franky's performance is a grab bag of little quirks and maladies.
reviews.author: A.S. Hamrah

reviews.text: Hirokazu aims to make us reflect over the significance of family in society. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Iván Belmont

reviews.text: This is a stunning demonstration of Hirokazu Koreeda's cinematic mastery. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fernanda Solórzano

reviews.text: .. the film delivers one gut punch after another, guaranteeing that Shoplifters will sit with you long after you finish watching it.
reviews.author: Michelle Jaworski

reviews.text: Japanese drama about unconventional family has mature themes
reviews.author: Barbara Shulgasser

reviews.text: The pace is slow and studied, but Hirokazu rewards your patience with a doozy of an ending that makes you reexamine what you've just seen without ever feeling the least bit gimmicky.
reviews.author: Rubén Rosario

reviews.text: Kore-eda elicits poignant performances from everyone in his ensemble, chose to accentuate the positive rather than dwell on the hardships.
reviews.author: M. Faust

reviews.text: This may sound like the basis for an especially indigestible bit of treacle, but the great filmmaker Hirokazu Kore-eda has more on his mind than that -- even as he is doling out passages of quietly exquisite beauty.
reviews.author: Peter Sobczynski

reviews.text: That the compassion comes from characters who exist on the fringes of accepted society only emphasizes the heartbreaking irony of Koreeda's message.
reviews.author: Dan Webster

reviews.text: It's the most fun Kore-eda has been in years, but also teaches some tough lessons.
reviews.author: Tom Bond

reviews.text: Like an unfolded origami flower that divulges its wrinkles, Writer/Director Hirokazu Kore-Eda reveals to Western viewers a non-traditional perspective of living in Japan.
reviews.author: Wendy Shreve

reviews.text: The virtues of those who are legally criminals contrasted with the obtuseness of those enforcing the status quo poses a conundrum for the viewer, as well as a bit of cinematic poetry.
reviews.author: Andrea Chase

reviews.text: In lesser hands the film would ask us to pity the Shibatas' impoverished plight. The way [Koreeda] presents them, however, has us basking in their independence, love, and joy.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: In its quiet, gentle way, "Shoplifters" builds to an emotional climax that's all the more devastating for the restraint that Kore-eda shows.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: The film runs counter to the idea that "you can't choose your family." It's a lovely concept Kore-eda explores with so much affection and joy, viewers will end up wanting to be a part of the Shibata family, too.
reviews.author: Kiko Martinez

reviews.text: This is actually a warm and loving family, and Kore-eda is as crafty as his principals in weaving together such an intriguing tale.
reviews.author: Bill Brownstein

reviews.text: Kore-eda's rich and poignant new family drama is almost disarmingly affecting (and effective), showcasing the height of the Japanese filmmaker's prowess.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: In Shoplifters, Koreeda builds his protagonists away from commiseration to show them all their vices and their discomforts. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Arantxa Luna

reviews.text: In the end, the power of Shoplifters is cumulative and unexpected. As with Osamu's tricks, legal and otherwise, it's only afterwards that you realize what has happened.
reviews.author: Alison Gillmor

reviews.text: The house is small and disorder prevails, but so does love and the enjoyment of a communal life: a mooring perhaps stronger than any blood tie. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Gaspar Zimerman

reviews.text: Koreeda especially knows how to film the child's clear cut point of view about the outside world. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Javier Porta Fouz

reviews.text: "Shoplifters" is complex, funny, joyful, sad and enthralling.
reviews.author: Brad Keefe

reviews.text: Another winner from...Hirokazu Kor-eeda. The story in many ways feels Dickensian- like a fresh take on Oliver Twist. I loved every performance.
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: A cinema that knows how to camouflage the urgency of its social denunciation under the edlicado approach to a series of daily odysseys. A question of pure humanity.
reviews.author: Manu Yáñez

reviews.text: An intelligent, profound, humanist and sensible film. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: If Satoshi Kon's Tokyo Godfathers pursued the 'lost, and then found child' narrative for general heartwarming effect, Shoplifters pivots into darker, more subtle territory.
reviews.author: Malik Adán

reviews.text: Honest stories like this allow us to rediscover our origin, where life happens spontaneously. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Laura Pacheco Mora

reviews.text: Shoplifters is another sterling example in showing the hopeful living in hopelessness, thanks to the humanistic view of its three-dimensional characters, the assured interweaving of heartfelt drama and a top-notch cast working at the top of their game.
reviews.author: Harris Dang

reviews.text: Never once is this a story that obstructs its telling to show off skill and craft, always technically nuanced and always engrossing.
reviews.author: Bill Arceneaux

reviews.text: A surprisingly sentimental choice for the Cannes Palme d'Or, this Japanese tale of a make-do family is a big warm hug of a movie.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: If [writer-director Hirokazu] Koreeda's film sometimes recalls a Victorian novel in its tactics - Victor Hugo would be proud - it earns every pull on the old heartstrings.
reviews.author: Margot Harrison

reviews.text: 10 Best of 2018: Honorable Mention.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: Shoplifters quickly becomes one of the most heartwarming and gratifying pieces of cinema from 2018.
reviews.author: Alan French

reviews.text: Writer-director Hirokazu Kore-eda fills the film with grace notes, humor and fine observations, circling and filling out each character while leaning more on innocence than corruption.
reviews.author: Tom Long

reviews.text: It's the perfect depiction of the line between being a good person and being law-abiding, and how that's not a border, but a Venn diagram.
reviews.author: Richard Whittaker

reviews.text: It would be trite to say "Shoplifters" steals the audience's heart. It's also inaccurate, because Kore-Eda and his charming ensemble cast of rogues put in the hard work to earn the audience's respect and affection.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: An unmitigated disaster virtually from beginning to end...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: Kore-eda's warm and naturalistic aesthetic style, which revels in capturing the magic of everyday activities... bonds us to the Shibatas before we even have time to question the morality of what they do.
reviews.author: Maximilian Von Thun

reviews.text: A quiet movie made with absolute confidence and no need to prove itself.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: Hirokazu Kore-eda's new film is the sleeper hit of 2018. The Japanese filmmaker has become a master of humanity, his films are true reflections of how we as flawed individuals are embraced by those closest to us, family.
reviews.author: Joe Friar

reviews.text: In the end, perhaps the most frustrating - and devastating - thing about Shoplifters is that if leaves us just as confused about what is right as the characters.
reviews.author: Marisa Carpico

reviews.text: Kore-eda marshals his considerable talents to tell what initially appears to be another story of family love and perseverance in the margins of society.
reviews.author: Ben Croll

reviews.text: Shoplifters is held up by the strength of its ensemble and Kore-eda's gifts as a storyteller, which gain with every movie he makes-even in the same year.
reviews.author: Andy Crump

reviews.text: This kind of subtle richness is not new for Kore-Eda, though it's as satisfying here as it's ever been.
reviews.author: Emily Yoshida

reviews.text: Kore-eda is at his best when he's suppressing his sentimentality, not when he's indulging it, but like his characters, fans of this inspired filmmaker must learn to take the good with the bad.
reviews.author: Ben Sachs

reviews.text: It's all beautifully done, if seemingly aimless; for most of its two-hour runtime, the joy of the movie lies mostly in watching these fine actors build their beautifully flawed and lived-in characters.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: Shoplifters is littered with wry humor and is refreshingly free of judgment.
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: At once charming and heart-wrenching, this exquisitely performed film will steal the hearts of both art-house and mainstream audiences.
reviews.author: Maggie Lee

reviews.text: Shoplifters achieves that ultimate goal of art as expressed by the artist Robert Filliou: It's art that makes life more interesting than art.
reviews.author: Inkoo Kang

reviews.text: It may be a story about an unusual family, but its statements about that family feel universal.
reviews.author: Mark Harrison

reviews.text: Shoplifters simply sits back, looks you quietly in the eye, and follows up every one of your judgements with "Yeah, but why?"
reviews.author: Andrew Todd

reviews.text: It's a new landmark in humanist cinema.
reviews.author: Stephen Rebello

reviews.text: There are numerous tender, affecting moments en route to the finale's tearjerker overdrive, many of them productively tangential to the overarching idea of choosing one's own family.
reviews.author: Mike D'Angelo

reviews.text: Might be his best picture yet.
reviews.author: Ken Eisner

reviews.text: A moving meditation on what truly constitutes the meaning of family.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: If Shoplifters had been made by almost any other filmmaker in the world, it could've been a maudlin debacle. In the hands of Koreeda, it's one of the finest and most genuinely moving motion pictures of the year.
reviews.author: Andrew Parker

reviews.text: Shoplifters is a revelation, its heartwarming, profound and devastating.
reviews.author: Anne Brodie

reviews.text: Hirokazu Koreeda is an artisan of empathy...and his gorgeously-shot and perfectly-acted Palme d'Or-winner film Shoplifters fits well within his pantheon of masterpieces.
reviews.author: Joel Mayward

reviews.text: Sincere and heartbreaking.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: The movie shows beauty in the characters' lives without making poverty look idyllic, but it doesn't patronize them either.
reviews.author: Hannah Lynn

reviews.text: It is a deeply sad mosaic of good people who are ultimately defined by the bad they've done, whether fairly or not... It remains up to filmmakers like Kore-eda to remind us that people are never this simple.
reviews.author: Glenn Heath Jr.

reviews.text: There is one narrative thread that pushes credibility to its limit, but there is more in Shoplifters that resonates and rings true.
reviews.author: Gary Thompson

reviews.text: When it comes to talking about the family, [director Hirokazu Koreeda] takes the cake. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Daniel de Partearroyo

reviews.text: Shoplifters is a masterful film that will have you rethinking the definition of family.
reviews.author: Courtney Small

reviews.text: A deeply humane Japanese film that trusts its audience to untangle its complex, interweaving relationships and the powerful dilemmas that follow.
reviews.author: Damien Straker

reviews.text: A delirious and captivating introduction to a fantasy scattered throughout just enough to exude a supreme elegance while playing with our perceptions. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: That Kore-eda makes these people not only empathetic but lovable is a sizable achievement, though one that shouldn't be a surprise to anyone who's seen his earlier work.
reviews.author: Tricia Olszewski

reviews.text: Viewer patience gets rewarded with the meaningful twists in a powerful final act that lovingly defines what a real family is all about.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: A story whose ethical quandaries are presented with equal parts compassion and toughness.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: Every one of master Japanese filmmaker Hirokazu Kore-eda's movies breaks your heart in a different way.
reviews.author: Moira MacDonald

reviews.text: It is complex, subtle, devastating, surprising and totally brilliant.
reviews.author: Alexa Dalby

reviews.text: Shoplifters finds Kore-eda at his most human and humane, painting a tender yet unflinching look at the life of a family society has more or less forgotten.
reviews.author: Joshua Brunsting

reviews.text: The movie uses a domestic drama to illustrate larger and more compelling concerns about society in general.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: Another exemplar of Kore-eda's refulgent humanity, evident skill as a dramatist, and, perhaps most importantly of all, as a deceptively clever visual artist.
reviews.author: PJ Nabarro

reviews.text: It is a carefully and beautifully crafted work that appears to be about one thing (the strong bonds of family life), but is really about something else-the way a city forces us to invent our lives.
reviews.author: Charles Mudede

reviews.text: Like the rest of Kore-eda's canon, Shoplifters is a gently humorous and poignant work of art.
reviews.author: Caroline Madden

reviews.text: The performances, particularly by Sakura Andô as Nobuyo, are incredible and the script is something every writer wishes they wrote themselves.
reviews.author: Lorry Kikta

reviews.text: If the family is a natural masterpiece it is almost always a flawed masterpiece.
reviews.author: John McDonald

reviews.text: ...definitely goes after your heartstrings, yet earns any tears it gets.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: This movie makes a persuasive argument that it is love, not genetics, that makes a family.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: Shoplifters is well worth seeing for its twist-filled story and phenomenal acting.
reviews.author: Hannah Brown

reviews.text: It occurs to you that this is no mere movie; it's life itself, and all the messy heartbreak and beauty that entails.
reviews.author: Al Alexander

reviews.text: A family drama about a clan of grifters evolves into a crime mystery and a devastating indictment not of lawbreakers but of the system that fosters them .
reviews.author: Annlee Ellingson

reviews.text: In a great film, Kore-eda's thesis would be the starting point, not its culmination... But in the end, Kore-eda, for all the cooked-up moments in Shoplifters, knows where the heart of his story is.
reviews.author: Peter Rainer

reviews.text: About an hour in things begin to unravel, undercutting the audience's assumptions and steadily accumulating great weight and moral severity. By the time it ended I was a wreck.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: Overflowing with warmth without lurching into sentimentality, emotional but never manipulative, "Shoplifters" asks what makes a family, and how an unorthodox one can survive within the structures of society. (Just don't watch on an empty stomach.)
reviews.author: Sarah Cartland

reviews.text: Shoplifters is an astonishing, heartbreaking film that offers no easy answers to the questions that it raises.
reviews.author: Chloe Schama

reviews.text: It's in theory the worst family movie of 2018 - and in practice one of the year's best films.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: Kore-eda's script is laced with small moments of affection to build a story so utterly grounded by love that the novelty of the crimes they commit feels secondary.
reviews.author: Matthew Dougherty

reviews.text: What makes it such an enrapturing experience is the tenderness, humour and detail [director Hirokazu] Kore-eda brings to his material.
reviews.author: Geoffrey Macnab

reviews.text: Another Kore-eda tale of hard-pressed individuals struggling to live "normal" lives in spite of it all. Get out your handkerchiefs.
reviews.author: Kelly Vance

reviews.text: The entire cast is phenomenal, with a lived-in chemistry.
reviews.author: Allyson Johnson

reviews.text: The spirits of the old masters pervade this disquieting but deeply moving drama. But Kore-eda stands alone as the chronicler of family life in a country facing an identity crisis.
reviews.author: David Parkinson

reviews.text: For Kore-eda, money unavoidably gives reliance on each other the appearance of abuse, even in the eyes of the kindest shoplifter. Doubt takes over, and the herd disperses into lonely wolves, aggressive because they are scared of getting hurt again.
reviews.author: Manuela Lazic

reviews.text: conveys the messy, boisterous joy of three generations sharing and caring in close quarters and the ofttimes harsh residuals of justice.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: Delicately observed and perfectly played, it's consummate, flawless film-making.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: There is something distinctly Dickensian about the generosity of the director's vision, from that Fagin-like father to the warm miscellaneous clutter of their apartment, which Kore-eda shoots as snugly as if it were a child's playhouse.
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: Shoplifters is a film of rare depth and quality.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: It's deceptively simple, sweet, often funny, thought-provoking, moving but never mawkish and really accessible.
reviews.author: Aine O'Connor

reviews.text: Lingers in a murky area between cynicism and hope that makes its final moments a wrenching punch to the gut.
reviews.author: Leigh Monson

reviews.text: One of the best films of the year with its sensitive and soulful advocacy of kind-heartedness.
reviews.author: Frederic and Mary Ann Brussat

reviews.text: Kore-eda has sculpted a breathtakingly delicate exploration of what it means to find your tribe.
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: Skilled, nuanced storytelling and realistic pacing produce a graceful, textured, compelling portrait of a people with problematic behavior, shortchanged by circumstance, who interact lovingly.
reviews.author: Anita Katz

reviews.text: Koreeda expertly twists his usual pleasantries, giving us just enough to let us think this can last forever, buoyed by the innate certainty we bring to our daily lives.
reviews.author: Scott Nye

reviews.text: This is a film with no set pieces or major plot twists but it is wholly absorbing and it will steal your heart.
reviews.author: Deborah Ross

reviews.text: Kora-eda coaxes superb performances from the two child actors who never become cute moppets.
reviews.author: Saskia Baron

reviews.text: It's an eerily moving piece, masterfully blurring the divide between the unforgivable and understandable, finding tenderness in the bleakest and most traumatic of circumstances.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: As easy as it is to be appalled at the horrible conditions that caused this situation, it's just as easy to become involved with the characters and their little triumphs and tragedies.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: Kore-eda crafts a charming, bittersweet tale of a family's perseverance through tough times with their strong bond to one another, reinforced by their strong personalities.
reviews.author: Adam Patterson

reviews.text: Though we never untangle the difference between right and wrong in Shoplifters, we find ourselves emotionally invested in this inescapable work of art.
reviews.author: Robert Daniels

reviews.text: ... maintains a firm grasp on the moral complexity of its subject matter with a portrayal that feels both socially conscious and humanely authentic.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: If you have the patience to stick out the slow pace, you'll find a lot of meaning inside this slice-of-life story.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: Kore-eda manages to turn the family's boxy, claustrophobic living quarters into a refuge, and the film's buoyant soundtrack exudes more whimsy than woe.
reviews.author: Randall Colburn

reviews.text: Shoplifters is a heart-warming examination of domestic poverty in Tokyo, and a modern Dickensian masterpiece worthy of its Palme d'Or award.
reviews.author: Lewis Knight

reviews.text: This film is about the good and bad that co-exist in people, perhaps in all of us.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: The film creeps up on you. It yields its pleasures stealthily. It has, however, more to say about questions of public and private morality than whole libraries.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: Kore-eda has the sensitive, calibrated touch of a master safecracker, and he's a virtuoso of emotional and narrative buildup.
reviews.author: Manohla Dargis

reviews.text: What really makes this special is the sheer depth of compassion and knowing humanity behind every frame.
reviews.author: Trevor Johnston

reviews.text: Shoplifters tells a deceptively simple story that gradually reveals layers ... about its characters, their pasts, their relationships, and how ... we connect as people.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: The brilliance of the film comes from the way Koreeda quietly and non-judgmentally observes this clan up close as they care for and look out for one another before gradually pulling back to reveal the true nature of their various relationships.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: A spirited, lilting delight.
reviews.author: Beth Webb

reviews.text: Beautifully played by the whole cast, from the five Shibatas to the tiny Sasaki as Yuri to even the bit actors with one line, this is, as Koreeda hoped, all about family, in whatever form it might take.
reviews.author: David 'Mad Dog' Bradley

reviews.text: This wise and insightful film is delicate, poignant and unexpectedly powerful.
reviews.author: Kenneth Turan

reviews.text: This soft-spoken, cinematic treasure about a family of thieves highlights the quietly devastating artistry of Japanese master Hirokazu Kore-eda. It's impossible to experience the deep-seated compassion of this film and not be moved to tears.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: If Shoplifters asks huge questions about what a family is and is not, the answers are hinted at in fleeting gestures - the hallmark of this beautiful, ambiguous film.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: Shoplifters, overall is a slow but captivating burn that may leave you questioning your own hard-set ideas of right, wrong and family.
reviews.author: Lindsey Bahr

reviews.text: Shoplifters is an absorbing, masterful film that opens out like a Japanese fan into a coda of sociological commentary that will leave you pondering about the ethics of families and their brands of dysfunction, veiled and visible alike,
reviews.author: Paddy Kehoe

reviews.text: Shoplifters is so tender and meticulous about establishing the cramped, desperate and insular world of these characters that you're hardly prepared for the emotional punch of the film's final act.
reviews.author: Daniel Barnes

reviews.text: This is so beautifully observed that cast members never seem to be acting.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: As with Kore-eda's previous efforts, which also include Like Father, Like Son and After the Storm, Shoplifters is a sumptuous-looking, languidly paced, lovingly created gentle drama that deceptively packs a powerful narrative punch.
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: Members of a family living on state support are not what they seem in an award-winning drama from Hirokazu Kore-eda.
reviews.author: Daniel Eagan

reviews.text: Not only is it warmly accessible thanks to the pulsing humanity of its performances, but its story goes far beyond tender-hearted social realism into darker and more morally challenging territory.
reviews.author: Hannah McGill

reviews.text: Kore-eda, in his steady and unhectoring way, is levelling grave accusations at Japanese social norms, yet what stays with you, unforgettably, is that bundle of mixed souls at the start.
reviews.author: Anthony Lane

reviews.text: Both a gentle examination of what constitutes a real family and a harsh dissection of Japan's faltering social landscape.
reviews.author: David Lewis

reviews.text: This ragtag Japanese family is so charming you might hope the shoplifters will never get caught.
reviews.author: Harvey S. Karten

reviews.text: Hirokazu Kore-eda imbues his characters with so much empathy, no matter what they do (and some of it is quite questionable), you don't judge them, you understand.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: The final 30 minutes will tear your heart out, with the last five or so especially stomping on it for good measure, effectively driving home the complicated questions regarding family Kore-eda is posing
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: The director's deceptively simple treatment ensures that Shoplifters is an unsentimental heart-warmer of considerable charm and insight.
reviews.author: David Stratton

reviews.text: The film feels like a nice, warm hug. Its energy and empathy are infectious. Kore-eda manages to tell both a compelling narrative and a slice of life human story all in one.
reviews.author: Christopher James

reviews.text: Shoplifters does something beautiful: it reminds you how love - or the memory of it - is a powerful consolation for the tough times that inevitably come.
reviews.author: Jason Di Rosso

reviews.text: Observed with tender, telling detail, their lives spill out of the overcrowded home in much the same way that a need for caring and connection spills out from their hearts.
reviews.author: Craig Mathieson

reviews.text: Shoplifters is a film of radical compassion...
reviews.author: Chris Feil

reviews.text: With an exactingly tender touch, filmmaker Hirokazu Kore-eda delivers nothing short of a masterpiece - and perhaps also a career best.
reviews.author: Courtney Howard

reviews.text: A heartfelt socially- conscious Naruse-like gentle family drama by the talented humanist Japanese filmmaker Hirokazu Koreeda.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: The plot revelations, which [director Hirokazu] Kore-eda cunningly piles up at the end, are heartbreaking when they hit.
reviews.author: Stuart Klawans

reviews.text: One of the most sublimely realised character studies Kore-eda has ever produced.
reviews.author: Alistair Ryder

reviews.text: Kore-eda takes the time to affectionately dissect the way family functions, before carefully deconstructing it and revealing the contoured complexities that live within.
reviews.author: Jordan Ruimy

reviews.text: If there is a cinematic equivalent of comfort food, Koreeda's movies are it and Shoplifters is one of the best examples.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: The ending breaks the heart and makes you think hard about the ties that bind us.
reviews.author: Baradwaj Rangan

reviews.text: The well laid out setup-rickety home, poor neighborhood and lively clan who lives off their grandma's gov't check-makes you think their brushes with the law and experiences with irate shopkeepers will lead somewhere. It doesn't.
reviews.author: Dwight Brown

reviews.text: Deceptively profound and filled with great performances, Shoplifters is yet another Kore-eda triumph.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: In true Kore-eda fashion the film is quietly devastating, slowly accumulating an avalanche of emotions that climaxes in a beautiful sequence.
reviews.author: Nathanael Hood

reviews.text: "Maybe the bond is stronger when you choose your family," says someone, and darned if the film doesn't make a good case for that notion.
reviews.author: Bob Mondello

reviews.text: Revealing this delicate story's surprises would not only be unkind but would also misleadingly suggest that the director's intentions are of a shock-and-awe-ish variety. Kore-eda is interested, first and foremost, in the definition of family.
reviews.author: Nick Schager

reviews.text: Kore-eda is a masterful storyteller. Just as we're complacent and pleased with how this peculiar family goes on, secrets begin to spill... Layer by layer we're led into stark, riveting realism.
reviews.author: Diana Cheng

reviews.text: Kore-eda navigates this reality with a graceful perceptiveness, a subtle humor, and an inspired precision that never compromises the humanity of his subjects.
reviews.author: Tomas Trussow

reviews.text: One of the best films at TIFF this year, if not simply one of the best films of the year, period.
reviews.author: Karen Han

reviews.text: It's complex, touching...a fine art.
reviews.author: Lisa Nesselson

reviews.text: A compact masterpiece about a scruffy family that isn't what it seems, and love that's the real thing.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: Sometimes, the films of the Japanese master Hirokazu Kore-eda remind me of the novels of Paul Auster, deceptively simple prose that builds slowly into a puzzle piece of quietly explosive force.
reviews.author: Simon Houpt

reviews.text: For the bulk of 'Shoplifters,' Kore-eda works in a beautiful register that feels both detailed and genuine at the same time.
reviews.author: Brian Tallerico

reviews.text: As this apparently amoral group reveals its collective heart, Shoplifters gets richer and warmer, building to an ending that's no less powerful for being so very small.
reviews.author: Norman Wilner

reviews.text: Shoplifters is so gently observed and generous and careful with its characters that when misfortune finally befalls this family group, it's almost unbearable to watch.
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: In Shoplifters, writer-director Hirokazu Kore-eda dramatizes the insidious and relativistic ordinariness of poverty.
reviews.author: Chuck Bowen

reviews.text: Sex, love, puberty and even death are all handled with a refreshing level of honesty, never letting a life lesson become a big moment, but rather another step in growing up, a true reflection on the way real life works.
reviews.author: Alex Lines

reviews.text: Koreeda provides us with another exemplary portrait of hopeful people in hopeless situations.
reviews.author: Nicholas Bell

reviews.text: Shoplifters is built on an outrageously melodramatic plot, but in Kore-eda's hands, it comes off as natural, touching and genuine.
reviews.author: Kong Rithdee

reviews.text: This is Kore-eda at his most subtle, nuanced and morally inquiring.
reviews.author: Stephanie Bunbury

reviews.text: Where Shoplifters ultimately goes is at once unexpected and inevitable, arriving at a startling, powerful conclusion that is carried on the back of one of the strongest screen ensembles in years.
reviews.author: Tom Augustine

reviews.text: The film derives it gut-wrenching emotional power from just how spare it is.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: As an observer of the various dimensions and dynamics of families, [director Kore-eda Hirokazu] is a modern master.
reviews.author: Mallory Andrews

reviews.text: Koreeda's quiet, angry masterpiece reaffirms once again that no other filmmaker working today has a better understanding of - or compassion for - families.
reviews.author: James Marsh

reviews.text: [Few directors] have succeeded in granting a parallel and generational role to their characters, and that is precisely what makes Hirokazu Koreeda's new film, Shoplifters, a wonderful... compendium about the ethics of crime. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alberto Sáez Villarino

reviews.text: Kore-eda, who trained as a documentary filmmaker and once aspired to be a novelist, inserts lines that illuminate and pierce, while masterfully building to a climax stronger in reflection than the moment.
reviews.author: Mark Schilling

reviews.text: Kore-eda's gentle drama about a made-up "family" of thieves living on the margins of society is shot through with the director's trademark generosity and attention to behavior.
reviews.author: Bilge Ebiri

reviews.text: Another charming, funny and very affecting example of Kore-eda's special brand of tough-but-tender humanism.
reviews.author: Geoff Andrew

reviews.text: Pinpointing the bottom of society and finding in supposedly the worst of Japan that which in fact makes it best.
reviews.author: Daniel Kasman

reviews.text: A worthy winner of the 2018 Palme d'Or, this is a compassionate and complicated love letter to family and the secrets and lies which accompany them.
reviews.author: Jo-Ann Titmarsh

reviews.text: In a less composed director's hands, this would be sentimental guff. Here, it's potent.
reviews.author: Gus Edgar

reviews.text: Shoplifters showcases one of the modern cinema's great empaths deploying compassion like a time-delay nerve agent; this is Koreeda's expansive humanism, weaponised.
reviews.author: Jessica Kiang

reviews.text: In an impeccable alchemy, [director Hirokazu] Koreeda mixes [the film's] ingredients: the legal, the ethical, the emotional, the blood ties. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Juanma Ruiz

reviews.text: In his latest film, [director Hirokazu Koreeda presents a family that lives in marginalization. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Àngel Quintana

reviews.text: The filmmaker's clean, transparent and empathetic look... is manifested here with full harmony even when, starting from an unexpected accident, they begin to manifest themselves. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos F. Heredero

reviews.text: The story hardens, even obscures, but the writing and the style used are effective and end up convincing us completely. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: What it lacks in newness it makes up in raw humanity.
reviews.author: David Ehrlich

reviews.text: A complex, subtle, mysterious film that builds to the most extraordinary surprise ending, a twist-reveal worthy of psychological suspense noir.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: Who better than Kore-eda, a director who whispers instead of shouts, is able to capture contradictions and issues though such a subtle, unforced style of storytelling?
reviews.author: Deborah Young

reviews.text: Shoplifters is compassionate, socially conscious filmmaking with a piercing intelligence that is pure Kore-eda. This is a film that steals in and snatches your heart.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: We are confronted with a steely critique of society's (and humanity's) failings - one not seen in the director's work, with this level of clarity, since his quietly devastating 2004 work Nobody Knows.
reviews.author: Lee Marshall

synopsis: On the margins of Tokyo, a dysfunctional band of outsiders is united by fierce loyalty and a penchant for petty theft. When the young son is arrested, secrets are exposed that upend their tenuous, below-the-radar existence.
